targets.authors: Suzuki, K., Lush, P., Seth, A. K., & Roseboom, W.
targets.title: Intentional binding without intentional action.
targets.evidence_quote: We performed a conceptual replication of Suzuki et al.’s (2019) Experiment 1, with one key alteration: instead of using a random sequence for presenting temporal intervals, we employed a block design to potentially reduce the effect of regression toward the mean.
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, the experiments reported in the current study consistently replicated the effect between active and no hand trials, as reported by Suzuki et al. (2019). This comparison represents the typical passive vs active contrast, tested in many studies about temporal binding, that has been interpreted as evidence that intentional actions underpin the observed temporal compression (Moore & Obhi, 2012).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly confirm the active/no-hand comparison but explicitly contrast active/fake-hand results with Suzuki in all three experiments. The abstract failures refer to the central contrast rather than an overall verdict covering all tested findings.
targets.outcome_additional_quote: In both these experiments, the data consistently showed a more pronounced temporal compression in active trials, contrasting with the findings presented by Suzuki et al. (2019).

reasoning: New participants in three experiments re-test Suzuki Experiment 1. Other references motivate or explain the study rather than being targets. The discussion reports agreeing and disagreeing comparisons.
